title: Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
summary: Given an array of integers and a threshold, find the smallest divisor where the sum of the ceiling division results of each element by the divisor is less than or equal to the threshold.
statement: Given an array of integers and a threshold, find the smallest divisor where the sum of the ceiling division results of each element by the divisor is less than or equal to the threshold. Each division result is rounded up.
constraints: nums is positive and threshold >= len(nums).
Find the smallest positive divisor whose rounded-up quotient sum is at most threshold.
reference_solution:
def smallest_threshold_divisor(nums, threshold):
 left,right=1,max(nums)
 while left<right:
  middle=(left+right)//2
  if sum((x+middle-1)//middle for x in nums)<=threshold:right=middle
  else:left=middle+1
 return left

hints: The quotient sum never increases as the divisor grows.
Binary-search divisors from one through max(nums).
Use integer ceiling (x+d-1)//d and keep feasible midpoints on the right.
Monotonic feasibility makes the first feasible divisor well-defined.
